evidence: Manifest ships index.svg and has no lifecycle scripts or dependencies.

Read the complete SVG. Inline code adapts DOM calls to the foreignObject XHTML namespace, mirrors attributes, configures disclosed proxy endpoints, initializes Google Analytics, and dismisses a splash screen.
Remote query-bearing script is Google Analytics. The advertised cloaking/panic controls do not collect credentials or deceive the user about the application's purpose.

evidence: UPX checksum fails. Emulated only the decompression/branch-repair stub with Unicorn, stopping at 0x42871c before import resolution or application execution.

Rizin recovered main 0x4013a0: reads its own image, finds [[UNIQUE]], randomizes 16 bytes, writes a clone, submits file[]/node/submit form fields through libcurl, deletes the clone and repeats after Sleep(30000). Node choice is restricted to NODE1 through NODE7.
The historical endpoint was a public, opt-in upload-and-execute VM playground. Self-submission alone does not establish unauthorized propagation.
The appended PE is included in the self-image upload but is not launched by the recovered application. No discovered theft, spying, destruction, backdoor, or downloaded execution.
A published Snojan DLL analysis describes a different downloader; that family name does not establish this program's behavior.

evidence: Stock upx -d successfully recovered a 763480-byte ELF. Rizin main at 0x401730 sets signal handlers, initializes an XOR-0x54 string table and a controller sockaddr, then receives length-prefixed controller messages.
Attack parser 0x402440 consumes vector, duration, target and option fields; 0x402380 forks a timed attack worker and selects an attack function from a method table.
Scanner at 0x409440 creates a raw IPv4 socket and sends SYN probes. The scanner sets port 23 at 0x40b5d8 and maintains login/password states with a device-default credential table.

XOR-0x54 decoding exposes 7ujMko0admin, 7ujMko0vizxv, hi3518, watchdog paths, login dialogue and Source Engine Query. The watchdog/device constants and VSE request alone are not sufficient to prove malicious intent.
